author: Craig Sesker Leader-Telegram reporter
title: Struggles continues as Express falls again at home - NewsBreak
text: It was a frustrating finish as the struggles continue for the Eau Claire Express. Eau Claire had a runner picked off first base to end the game in a 9-7 loss to Duluth on Wednesday night at Carson Park. The Express fell to 5-12 in Northwoods League baseball play. Eau Claire has dropped four straight games and eight of its last nine. "We're not playing really good, solid baseball," Express manager Dale Varsho said. "We had five walks where those runners all scored. We have to shore up a lot of things to make sure we are a good, competitive team." Eau Claire connected for five runs in the fourth inning to grab a 7-3 lead. Express third baseman Ian Guanzon highlighted the inning by crushing a mammoth three-run homer to left-center field. "That was a huge home run," Varsho said. "Ian came through in a big spot and gave us the lead." Eau Claire starter Easton Bobb was in position to earn the win before the Huskies rallied. Bobb, a left-hander from Chippewa Falls, went 5 2/3 innings on Wednesday. He walked six and struck out two while allowing six earned runs. "For his standards, it was pretty mediocre," Varsho said of Bobb's outing. "He was probably pretty mad about his start. He's been really good for us and has pitched well. What I like about him is he competes out there and gives us a good start every time." Left fielder Marcelino Alonso went 2-for-5, scored twice and drove in three runs for the Express. Eau Claire shortstop Alex Hendrickson continues to excel. He had three hits Wednesday. Express reliever Dylan Dickert was outstanding in pitching three scoreless and hitless innings. He retired all nine batters he faced, striking out four and walking none. The Express are still trying to find the right combination as players continue to come and go on the Eau Claire roster. "We have to be better in all aspects of the game," Varsho said. "We need to stop walking guys and make them earn it. Those walks are killing us. "We got to get more people in here and keep getting after it." Subscribe to the Leader Telegram
